sources.access_depth: full PDF
sources.locator: Articles4-6 / PDF pp.3-4

sources.access_depth: full PDF
sources.locator: historical map methods and mound inventory; online25 December2018 / volume2019
sources.observation: Historical Survey of India maps preserve lost mound information. The cartographic record and its selective symbols are prior research, not a new method introduced here.

sources.observation: 779 map features were checked;199 yielded archaeological material;169 were unlinked to earlier reports;64 additional locations were off-map. Counts span periods. Table percentages permit unique integer recovery.

sources.title: Counter-intuitive influence of Himalayan river morphodynamics on Indus Civilisation urban settlements
sources.access_depth: full PDF
sources.locator: Results and discussion: palaeo-Sutlej avulsion chronology
sources.observation: Sutlej abandonment of the studied Ghaggar-Hakra course shortly after8ka predates urban Indus occupation. It does not date every local channel or exclude later monsoon-fed flows.

sources.title: Larger floods of Himalayan foothill rivers sustained flows in the Ghaggar–Hakra channel during Harappan age
sources.access_depth: full PDF; publication metadata checked
sources.locator: JQS36(4):611-627; accepted20 April2021; Markanda flood chronology
sources.observation: Foothill palaeofloods around3.9-3.8ka indicate episodic Ghaggar-Hakra flow in a later period. Local filename and URL say2020; actual article is2021.

sources.title: Fluvial landscapes of the Harappan civilization
sources.access_depth: full primary article read through web tool; local HTML download was a challenge and excluded
sources.locator: Results; Indus fluvial ridge and regional river histories
sources.observation: Settlement distribution and river-landscape stability vary regionally. A present river or empty modern floodplain is an incomplete guide to Bronze Age occupation.

sources.title: Use of Satellite SAR for Understanding Long-Term Human Occupation Dynamics in the Monsoonal Semi-Arid Plains of North Gujarat, India
sources.access_depth: full PDF
sources.locator: methods; ENVISAT seasonal comparison; dune/interdune archaeological settings
sources.observation: Seasonal radar water mapping helps interpret dune/interdune landscapes of lower Banas, Saraswati and Rupen. Current water patterns require independent ancient environmental dates.

sources.title: Archaeological Explorations at the Harappan Site of Kotada in Lodrani, Bela Bet, Gujarat

sources.observation: Kotada identified before2024 Morodharo announcement; names refer to the same locality.100×60m fort is0.6ha, not the whole site. Early/Mature evidence coexists with later material.

sources.observation: Later industrial expansion and dumping removed upper layers, while lower craft and seal-workshop evidence survived. Account supports targeted urban rescue work, not an authenticated300ha boundary.

sources.observation: Quarry and extraction landscapes extend archaeological activity beyond settlement mounds. Associated camps and transport traces require their own evidence and chronology.

sources.observation: Village ceramic economies and craft organization show that small settlement area alone does not measure social or economic complexity.

sources.title: Evidence for Seawater Retreat With Advent of Meghalayan Era (∼4200 a BP) in a Coastal Harappan Settlement
sources.access_depth: primary abstract and first-page PDF; full article not obtained
sources.locator: abstract;23:e2021GC010264
sources.observation: Lothal sediment proxies indicate relative sea-level fall beginning4150±230BP and continuing to3625±200BP. Local interpretation does not establish universal sea-level history or settle dock function.

sources.title: Extremely fast Holocene coastal landscape evolution in the Kachchh Upland (NW India): Clues from a multidisciplinary review
sources.access_depth: full published PDF obtained from University of Palermo
sources.locator: abstract; mapped deltaic-alluvial fans and Northern Hill Range
sources.observation: Regional shallow marine landscapes became inland salt desert through interacting tectonic, climatic and sedimentary changes. Some former coastal targets are now inland.

sources.title: Holocene relative sea-level history of the Gulf of Khambhat, Western India: Revisiting regional records with standardized SLIP protocols
sources.access_depth: primary publisher-indexed abstract/introduction and Crossref metadata; full text unavailable
sources.locator: Quaternary International759:110163; March2026
sources.observation: Only Lothal/Vadgam satisfy full sea-level index-point criteria in this synthesis; some other indicators are limiting or tectonically influenced. Proxy indicative meaning and uncertainty matter.
